editorial:
Imagine going to a funeral for an old buddy, only to realize that the guy in the casket might not be the only thing hiding a secret. You get to follow two old friends who show up to pay their respects to Pete Smalls, but the mood shifts quickly from sad to strange. It starts off as a slow-burn comedy where the banter between the leads feels like a real conversation you would have with your own best friend. The vibe is very laid-back at first, but it slowly turns into a mystery that keeps you wondering if you can actually trust anyone in the room.

What really works here is how the movie handles the surprises without feeling forced. The acting is natural and the pacing keeps you interested even when things seem quiet. While it might be a bit slow for some, the payoff is worth it if you enjoy quirky stories. If you are looking for a fun night in, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture. Or, if you like owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for a movie this unique.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that Pete Smalls is not actually dead in the way you think. The funeral was a giant setup to trick people and uncover secrets. After a series of funny and tense arguments, the truth comes out that the whole event was a prank and a test of loyalty. The friends realize they were played, but they end up closer because of the chaos. It wraps up with a laugh and a lesson on friendship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves low-key comedies with a twist.
